answer: The anchor is a sponsor registry, and one grove is one fake identity. It admits a grove only when one unrelated sponsor stakes it, and no sponsor may burn for another grove. Each sponsor burn must match population, one unit being one river. Adding the kth clone forces every current sponsor to top up and the new sponsor to burn k, so k clones cost k^2 river. Batch or split still costs k^2 because the registry prices final population, not arrival order. Call this sponsor-depth top-up. It breaks if the anchor lets one sponsor back another grove or exempts a sponsor from top-up.
